[Music] A thousand thanks to Mother Mary and Jesus. My name is Dr. Rosin Joseph. I am a
gynecologist and am currently working in Dubai. We have come back to our homeland for a vacation.
My home is in Chalakudy. I took the covenant in 2022. It was for the sake of my son.
At that time, I had already shared my testimony about him. This is my second testimony. I have
been working in my hometown since completing my NG in 2011. After that, I decided to apply to Dubai.
Due to some issues at my job, I had the need to move to Dubai. Then, the first thing I looked into was how to write the DHA Specialist
exam. It is one of the toughest exams. Because it had been 13–14 years since I last wrote an entrance
exam. So naturally, I had my fears and concerns about it. Since I was working as a gynecologist, I
did not have much time at all.
Being a gynecologist while working, I really did not have enough time.
So, I didn’t get any time to prepare at all. As my father always says, “Not by merit, but by grace” — that’s what happened in my case.
Because I had probably opened the book for just one day. After that, I went to write the exam. When I went to the exam, it was a three-hour exam.
When I reached there, I was told to submit my passport. I already knew that covenant medal could not be taken inside.
So, I had kept my medal in my pocket. I entered the exam center, knowing this, because it had been many years since I last wrote this exam.
I didn’t know anything about Dubai’s rules. But within one and a half hours, my exam was over.
Even then, I had no confidence about what would happen after this one and a half hours.
One and a half hours later, I finished the exam and came out.
A couple of days after that, I received my result. When the result came, I had passed.
So, to pass the DHA Specialist exam on the first attempt was a great blessing.
Indeed. After that, the intention in my covenant was the one I had taken for my second renewal.
The problem I had was that it was my first time going to work abroad.
Although I had studied in Bangalore, it was my first time going to a city like Dubai.
I was going there for the first time; I didn’t know anything and had no one there to help me, but I got a good
job at a clinic. So my next issue was that I needed an apartment because I wanted to take a maid to look after my children.
But according to the local rules,
I could not sponsor her unless I had a two-bedroom apartment. The next problem was that,
I was going to work in Karama, and the cost of an apartment in Karama —
— was quite high; a two-bedroom was very expensive compared to a studio.
The apartment was beyond what I could really consider at that time, so I just casually looked at an ad.
Then I found a very cheap two-bedroom apartment — it was available with one month’s rent in the lease.
I got that, but then a problem came up when I tried to get the Emirates ID — there was a delay in getting it.
I went to meet the apartment owner and spoke with her; usually a woman goes there to deal with these things.
After meeting her, I didn’t know whether she would agree to give me a one-month gap period.
I didn’t have a checkbook and my documents weren’t ready, but she was such a good person — a perfect example that the Blessed Mother is a pilgrim mother.
Wherever I went, everything was already arranged; I didn’t have to do anything myself.
After I went, the director told me, “Doctor, no problem — you’re a specialist, aren’t you? Don’t be afraid of being alone.
We will give the doctor as much time as needed. You don’t need to pay anything now.”
He said that if the Emirates side takes two months, then when that time comes the doctor can simply submit the check.
He told me that, and I felt it was a blessing.
After that, bringing the children over had its own sponsorship difficulties.
Once the sponsorship was done, the next difficulty was the children’s schooling.
I had always wanted the children’s school to be very near — ideally a school I could see just opposite my clinic when I opened the window.
Both of them got admission, and our apartment was just about 500 meters away — within walking distance.
When they joined, they were following the CBSE syllabus; later the school followed the UK syllabus, and I was afraid that the syllabus change would cause problems for my elder son.
I had real worry; we would pray in the morning and only then would I leave the children at school.
After praying and leaving them, I knew that Mother was always with them.
My elder son was studying well and performing excellently in extracurricular activities.
The younger son is a blessing from Mother — I had many complications when I was 38–39 years old, and Mother gave me this son.
He is four years old; I enrolled him in FS1 (pre-KG).
When we first arrived here he hadn’t attended school before. After starting, he seemed withdrawn and wasn’t talking to anyone at school.
He wasn’t writing. The teachers told the senior staff that he was neither writing nor speaking and that they should inform me.
When I went and saw, they explained that the UK syllabus has a particularity: if children are not writing or reading properly, they may be categorized as a special-needs child.
After that, bringing him up would be a terribly difficult thing. I was completely confused about what we should do.
So I thought, let’s go and pray to Mother with covenant salt.
The two of us — my sister and I — along with the aunt who looks after them, we together recited the Creed and prayed with the offering.
Since then I have not received a single complaint about him. He speaks well and studies well.
Both of them are performing well now. All of this happened while I was in the covenant.
After that, because I was in Dubai, I came back in December. In that November I had a problem: online scams were happening.
I didn’t know Dubai was a place where this could happen. By then only a few days had passed since my salary had come. My parents were in Dubai.
One day someone contacted me claiming to be from the Dubai police for verification, asking whether this was my Emirates ID and asking for all my details.
I had no suspicion at all. By God’s grace and Mother’s blessing, when they asked for the OTP I gave it.
At that moment I felt something was wrong, so I said, “Let it be verified.” I called my personal banker from another phone to ask if an OTP would be requested like this.
By then messages arrived saying all the money had been withdrawn from my bank. I didn’t know what to do because I didn’t know where to complain in Dubai.
My banker told me that once money is lost like that there is very little chance of getting it back — to consider it gone. Still, we said, “Let’s go to the bank and inquire.” We went to the bank.
Just before that I had gone into a supermarket and made a small purchase worth one dirham. I was holding the covenant medal tightly and crying as I walked there.
When I reached the bank, the officer told me, “Doctor, you are really lucky — God has saved you,” because when a cybercrime like this happens here there is almost no chance of getting money back.
I hadn’t lost even a single dirham — I couldn’t believe it. I thought, how could a lady like me manage these matters alone in Dubai? Very few people back home even know about this incident.
This was something I never expected to happen in Dubai. Later, concerning my son, there was a suspicion about a growth in his nose.
An evaluation was being done; there was concern he might need surgery. It was suspected to be adenoids — a growth in the nose.
But this time, because we were on vacation, we had him evaluated — there’s no serious problem. There’s only a slight issue in one part of his nose.
I always pray regularly for him. He has a nasal allergy, but there aren’t any major problems.
Still, no big issues. This boy also had two or three small lumps on his neck.
When you are a doctor, everything becomes a matter of doubt — everyone at home was worrying.
So my sister and I, along with the aunt who looks after them, would regularly count (our prayers) and pray for him so he would have no problems.
This child is a gift from Mother. I have some confidence that his Mother will watch over him.
I did blood tests and checked everything — all the results were normal.
They told me there was nothing to be concerned about in the way I was worrying. It was something like dandruff — a problem children sometimes get — nothing to panic about.
They advised not to be tense. I have had other experiences too, but to give the full testimony I should bring my father and mother next time when they come; then I will speak more.
As I said, I am currently working in Dubai, so I often ask my patients, “Do you believe?” These are the experiences I have had over many years.
Mother’s presence is in my clinic’s outpatient area. I tell my patients, “If you believe, pray to Mother — light a small candle and pray.”
Before I came here, two of my patients called me and said, “Madam, we are pregnant — please pray.” They asked me to light a candle and pray for them.
I was very happy about that. I hadn’t expected they would do that, because there are many restrictions here regarding missionary activity. So I mostly do devotional acts near my patients.
For charitable work, I give a fixed amount every month, and I try my best to help educate children where I can.
Throughout all this, Mother has always stood by me. Even though I am alone and only have my children, Mother
stands before all things. Problems do come, but I’ve seen them change and resolve before I even finish thinking about them.
So a thousand thanks to Mother, Jesus.
(Book of Hosea, chapter 14, verse 8) “I am like a perennial green tree; I will be to you a source of fruit.”.
The Holy Spirit is a great gift — wisdom and knowledge. We know that knowledge, understanding, and wisdom are gifts of the Holy Spirit.
Without the Holy Spirit’s special intervention, we would not receive these graces and be led into this place of mercy.
Father Joseph reminds us in every covenant meditation that without [this] we cannot lead covenant life forward.
He reminds us that even when we receive our daily bread, it is a great blessing given to us by the Father.
That daily nourishment — spiritual food for the whole day — is what the Father gives us so we may enter the Holy Mass and our everyday life.
All the children who are in the covenant, whatever their life situation, are watched over and cared for by the Blessed Mother. Surrendering all our affairs to Jesus is a great life-grace, everyone says.
Here Dr. Rosin spoke about the great miracles in her covenant life.
As an expatriate, she described how the Blessed Mother helped her bear all the hardships there, accompanied and blessed her throughout.
To pass the DHA Specialist exam — a three-hour exam — after a long gap in her studies was very stressful. Writing that test after such
a long break, burdened with life’s anxieties, she entrusted that whole exam time into the hands of the Blessed Mother. That is what the doctor testifies.
“It is not my merit but by grace” — this became very clear to me. When I surrender all my unworthiness, I see Jesus’ grace at work in me.
The doctor testifies that after she surrendered, she was able to finish a three-hour exam within one and a half hours.
We know that when the Blessed Mother appeared at this altar in 2004 she even showed the time on a clock. She
spoke about how the small and large things that unsettle us and threaten disaster are indeed things that can lead to disaster.
We hear testimony that, by appearing to us and entering our lives, she comforts us and shortens our time of trouble.
In Dr. Rosin’s family, all the children’s well-being, their behavioral manners, and their peace — the Blessed Mother protects this family through the covenant items used here.
Likewise, one of this sister’s great desires was to have a home very near her Dubai clinic. When we surrender our desires and needs to the Holy Mother and to Jesus,
when the Mother of God offers these to Jesus, today when this sister came and I opened my window...
When I opened my window, I could see my children’s school — it was only about 500 meters away.
The short distance between my school and home shows that this covenant arranges every part of our lives — it is a great life plan, as we can understand.
Likewise, when we are in a foreign country and money traps or problems arise back home,
she always comforts and helps us; she shows us ways to escape those situations without falling into them.
The Holy Spirit guides us — telling us what not to do, what to do, and which way to turn.
In the Gospel and in the Old Testament it is written, “I will tell you where to turn; I will instruct
you the way you should walk by looking upon your face” — the Lord God is graciously promising this to us.
For all our covenant life, more important than the blessings we receive is how we live the covenant — this is what every testimony emphasizes; it is the distinctive mark of our covenant life.
Likewise, if we live the covenant for three months here and then leave, perhaps when you decide to take the
covenant you will see answers for your situations — we know this comes as an incentive, as Father Joseph reminds us.
